key_insight: Training PV forecasting models to predict multiple future horizons at once improves long-term temporal learning and boosts accuracy beyond standard single-point forecasting.
engineering_relevance: This offers a scalable, low-overhead way to make solar power predictions more reliable, helping grid operators better manage PV intermittency and stability.
method: Combine ground-based sky images with historical PV output as input.
Use multi-horizon forecasting to jointly predict several future time steps.
Compare the approach across multiple deep learning architectures to show it is architecture-independent.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative evaluation across diverse deep learning models, with multi-horizon training improving accuracy and robustness over the full forecast window while adding negligible computational overhead.
watch_item: Performance gains may depend on the availability and quality of synchronized sky imagery and PV history, so real-world deployment needs careful data alignment and site-specific validation.
paper_title: Learning Long-Term Temporal Dependencies in Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction Through Multi-Horizon Forecasting
